question: Considering only the latest release versions for each distinct NPM package, which packages are the top 5 most popular based on the Github star number, as well as their versions?
agent_sql:
WITH stars AS (
  SELECT "Project_Information",
    lower(regexp_replace((regexp_match("Project_Information", '([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]*[A-Za-z0-9_-])'))[1], '\s',''))  AS slug,
    replace(COALESCE(
      (regexp_match("Project_Information", 'stars? count of ([0-9,]+)', 'i'))[1],
      (regexp_match("Project_Information", 'starred by ([0-9,]+)', 'i'))[1],
      (regexp_match("Project_Information", '([0-9,]+)\s+stars?', 'i'))[1]
    ), ',', '')::bigint AS star_count
  FROM deps_dev_v1_project_info
),
npm_pkgs AS (
  SELECT ppv."System", ppv."Name", ppv."Version", ppv."ProjectName", s.star_count
  FROM deps_dev_v1_project_packageversion ppv
  JOIN stars s ON lower(ppv."ProjectName") = s.slug
  WHERE ppv."System" = 'NPM' AND ppv."RelationType" = 'SOURCE_REPO_TYPE' AND ppv."Name" NOT LIKE '%>%'
),
joined AS (
  SELECT np.*, pi."UpstreamPublishedAt", pi."VersionInfo"
  FROM npm_pkgs np
  JOIN deps_dev_v1_packageinfo pi
    ON pi."System" = np."System" AND pi."Name" = np."Name" AND pi."Version" = np."Version"
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT *,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY "System","Name" ORDER BY "UpstreamPublishedAt" DESC NULLS LAST,
      (("VersionInfo"::jsonb)->>'Ordinal')::numeric DESC NULLS LAST, "Version" DESC) AS rn
  FROM joined
)
SELECT "Name" AS package, "Version" AS latest_version, star_count AS github_stars
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY star_count DESC, "Name"
LIMIT 5

plan.sources: deps_dev_v1_project_info.Project_Information holds owner/repo slug text and GitHub star counts in free text; deps_dev_v1_project_packageversion links (System,Name,Version) packages to a ProjectName (owner/repo) with a RelationType; deps_dev_v1_packageinfo holds UpstreamPublishedAt and VersionInfo (Ordinal) to determine the latest release per package.

plan.parse: star counts appear in three phrasings - 'stars? count of N', 'starred by N', 'N stars' (case-insensitive, comma-stripped) - covering all 770 rows; owner/repo slug captured via [A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]*[A-Za-z0-9_-] regex.
plan.filter: System='NPM'; RelationType='SOURCE_REPO_TYPE' (the actual source-repo relation, not issue tracker); Name NOT LIKE '%>%' to exclude transitive dependency-chain pseudo-names.
plan.metric: per (System,Name) pick the single latest release row ranked by UpstreamPublishedAt desc, then VersionInfo Ordinal desc, then Version string desc; star_count is the project's GitHub star count from Project_Information.
plan.rank: order candidate latest-release rows by star_count desc, tie-break by Name asc; take top 5 distinct packages.

question: Among all NPM packages with project license 'MIT' and marked as release, which 5 projects have the highest GitHub fork count?

WITH proj AS (
  SELECT
    "Project_Information",
    lower(substring("Project_Information" from '[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]*[A-Za-z0-9_-]')) as slug,
    replace(COALESCE(
      substring("Project_Information" from 'forks count of ([0-9,]+)'),
      substring("Project_Information" from 'forked ([0-9,]+) times'),
      substring("Project_Information" from '([0-9,]+) forks?')
    ), ',', '')::numeric as forks
  FROM deps_dev_v1_project_info
  WHERE "Licenses"::jsonb @> '["MIT"]'
),
pkg AS (
  SELECT p."System", p."Name", p."Version", pv."ProjectName"
  FROM deps_dev_v1_packageinfo p
  JOIN deps_dev_v1_project_packageversion pv
    ON p."System"=pv."System" AND p."Name"=pv."Name" AND p."Version"=pv."Version"
  WHERE p."System"='NPM'
    AND (p."VersionInfo"::jsonb->>'IsRelease')::boolean = true
)

FROM pkg pk
JOIN proj pr ON lower(pk."ProjectName") = pr.slug
GROUP BY pr.slug, pr.forks
ORDER BY pr.forks DESC

question: Among repositories that do not use Python, what proportion of their README.md files include copyright information?
answer: 0.1683 (17 out of 101 README.md files from non-Python repositories mention copyright)

with lang as (
  select repo_name, bool_or(language_description ~* '\mpython\M') as has_python
  from dataagentbench.github_repos_languages
  group by repo_name
),
readmes as (
  select c.id, c.sample_repo_name, c.content
  from dataagentbench.github_repos_contents c

question: Identify the repository that contains Swift code and the most frequently copied non-binary Swift (.swift) file in the dataset, ensuring that each file is uniquely determined by its ID in the files table.

question: Calculate the chi-square statistic to assess the association between histological types and the presence of CDH1 gene mutations in female BRCA patients from the PanCancer Atlas, excluding categories with marginal totals less than or equal to 10, and only focusing on patients with known histological types and consider only reliable mutation entries.
agent_sql:
WITH brca AS (
  SELECT patient_id,
    upper(substring("Patient_description" from 'TCGA-[A-Za-z0-9]+-[A-Za-z0-9]+')) AS barcode,
    histological_type
  FROM pancancer_atlas_clinical_info
  WHERE "Patient_description" ILIKE '%breast invasive carcinoma%'
    AND "Patient_description" ~ '\mFEMALE\M'
    AND histological_type IS NOT NULL
    AND histological_type !~ '^\[.*\]$'
),
mut AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT upper("ParticipantBarcode") AS barcode
  FROM pancancer_atlas_mutation_data
  WHERE "Hugo_Symbol" = 'CDH1' AND "FILTER" = 'PASS'
),
cells AS (
  SELECT b.histological_type,
    CASE WHEN m.barcode IS NOT NULL THEN 'mutated' ELSE 'not_mutated' END AS mut_status
  FROM brca b LEFT JOIN mut m ON b.barcode = m.barcode
),
row_tot AS (
  SELECT histological_type, count(*) rt FROM cells GROUP BY histological_type
),
col_tot AS (
  SELECT mut_status, count(*) ct FROM cells GROUP BY mut_status
),
kept_rows AS (SELECT histological_type FROM row_tot WHERE rt > 10),
kept_cols AS (SELECT mut_status FROM col_tot WHERE ct > 10),
grid AS (
  SELECT kr.histological_type, kc.mut_status,
    count(c.*) AS o
  FROM kept_rows kr
  CROSS JOIN kept_cols kc
  LEFT JOIN cells c ON c.histological_type = kr.histological_type AND c.mut_status = kc.mut_status
  GROUP BY kr.histological_type, kc.mut_status
),
rowsum AS (SELECT histological_type, sum(o) rs FROM grid GROUP BY histological_type),
colsum AS (SELECT mut_status, sum(o) cs FROM grid GROUP BY mut_status),
grand AS (SELECT sum(o) g FROM grid)
SELECT sum(power(g.o - (rs.rs*cs.cs::numeric/gr.g),2)/(rs.rs*cs.cs::numeric/gr.g)) AS chi_square
FROM grid g
JOIN rowsum rs ON rs.histological_type = g.histological_type
JOIN colsum cs ON cs.mut_status = g.mut_status
CROSS JOIN grand gr

plan.sources: pancancer_atlas_clinical_info.Patient_description (cohort text 'Breast invasive carcinoma', sex FEMALE, barcode), histological_type for the row category; pancancer_atlas_mutation_data.Hugo_Symbol='CDH1', FILTER, ParticipantBarcode for mutation presence column.
plan.keys: Match clinical patient barcode extracted from Patient_description (TCGA-xx-xxxx pattern, upper-cased) to mutation_data ParticipantBarcode (upper-cased) via LEFT JOIN so unmutated patients still appear.
plan.parse: Extract TCGA barcode via regex from Patient_description; extract FEMALE via word-boundary regex; histological_type used as-is excluding bracketed sentinel values like [Not Available].
plan.filter: Patient_description contains 'breast invasive carcinoma' (BRCA cohort) and FEMALE; histological_type is non-null and not a bracketed sentinel; mutation rows restricted to Hugo_Symbol='CDH1' and FILTER='PASS' (reliable calls).
plan.metric: 2-way contingency table: rows=histological_type, columns={mutated,not_mutated} presence of CDH1 mutation per patient; drop rows/columns whose marginal total <=10 computed on the full cell grid; chi-square = sum((O-E)^2/E) with E=row_total*col_total/grand_total computed over the surviving grid.
plan.rank: none - single aggregate statistic
plan.shape: one row, one column: chi_square value

agent_sql:
with recursive primary_cpc as (
  select pi.ctid as pid,
         left((elem->>'code'),4) as subclass,
         pi.filing_date
  from patents_publicationinfo pi,
       jsonb_array_elements(pi.cpc::jsonb) elem
  where (elem->>'first')::boolean = true
),
yearly as (
  select subclass,
         substring(filing_date from '\d{4}')::int as yr,
         count(distinct pid) as n
  from primary_cpc
  where substring(filing_date from '\d{4}') is not null
  group by subclass, substring(filing_date from '\d{4}')::int
),
ranges as (
  select subclass, min(yr) as miny, max(yr) as maxy from yearly group by subclass
),
years as (
  select r.subclass, gs as yr
  from ranges r, generate_series(r.miny, r.maxy) gs
),
filled as (
  select y.subclass, y.yr, coalesce(yl.n,0) as n
  from years y
  left join yearly yl on yl.subclass=y.subclass and yl.yr=y.yr
),
ema_calc as (
  select subclass, yr, n,
    row_number() over (partition by subclass order by yr) as rn
  from filled
),
recursive_ema as (
  select subclass, yr, n, n::numeric as ema, rn
  from ema_calc where rn=1
  union all
  select e.subclass, e.yr, e.n, (0.2*e.n + 0.8*r.ema) as ema, e.rn
  from ema_calc e
  join recursive_ema r on r.subclass=e.subclass and r.rn = e.rn-1
),
best as (
  select subclass, yr as best_year, ema,
    row_number() over (partition by subclass order by ema desc, yr asc) as rk
  from recursive_ema
)
select b.subclass as cpc_group_code, d."titleFull" as title, b.best_year, b.ema
from best b
join patents_cpc_definition d on d.symbol=b.subclass and d.level=5
where b.rk=1 and b.best_year=2022
order by b.subclass;

plan.sources: patents_publicationinfo.cpc (jsonb array elements with code/first) gives CPC classification codes per patent; filing_date gives the filing year text; patents_cpc_definition.symbol/level identify level-5 (4-char subclass) CPC group codes and their titles.
plan.keys: Derive subclass = left(code,4) from each primary (first=true) cpc element per patent; join subclass to cpc_definition.symbol where level=5 to restrict to valid level-5 group codes.
plan.parse: Extract the 4-digit filing year from filing_date text via regex \d{4} (format varies but always contains a 4-digit year).
plan.filter: Only cpc elements with first=true (primary classification) are counted; only rows with a parseable year are kept; each patent counted once per distinct subclass per year (count distinct patent ctid).

  from patents_publicationinfo
  where substring("Patents_info" from '(?:publication (?:number|no\.)|pub\. (?:number|no\.)) ([A-Z]{2})-') = 'DE'
),
h2 as (
  select *,
    substring(filing_date from '\d{4}')::int as f_year
  from base
  where g_year = '2019' and g_month3 in ('jul','aug','sep','oct','nov','dec')
),
patent_group as (
  select distinct h2."Patents_info", h2.f_year, left(elem->>'code',3) as grp
  from h2, jsonb_array_elements(h2.cpc::jsonb) elem
  where (elem->>'first')::bool = true
),
yearly as (
  select grp, f_year as yr, count(*) as n
  from patent_group
  group by grp, f_year
),
grp_range as (
  select grp, min(yr) as ymin, max(yr) as ymax from yearly group by grp
),
years as (
  select gr.grp, gs as yr
  from grp_range gr, generate_series(gr.ymin, gr.ymax) gs
),
filled as (
  select y.grp, y.yr, coalesce(yl.n,0) as n
  from years y
  left join yearly yl on yl.grp = y.grp and yl.yr = y.yr
),
ema_calc as (
  select grp, yr, n, n::numeric as ema, row_number() over (partition by grp order by yr) as rn
  from filled
  where yr = (select ymin from grp_range gr where gr.grp = filled.grp)
  union all
  select f.grp, f.yr, f.n, 0.1*f.n + 0.9*e.ema, e.rn+1
  from filled f
  join ema_calc e on e.grp = f.grp and f.yr = e.yr + 1
),
best as (
  select grp, yr, ema,
    row_number() over (partition by grp order by ema desc, yr asc) as rk
  from ema_calc
),
top as (
  select grp, yr as best_year, ema
  from best where rk = 1
),
maxema as (select max(ema) as m from top)
select t.grp as cpc_group_code, cd."titleFull" as full_title, t.best_year, t.ema as ema_value
from top t
join maxema m on t.ema = m.m
join patents_cpc_definition cd on cd.symbol = t.grp and cd.level = 4

## Sales Cycle Policy
- Definition: The sales cycle is measured as the number of days between an opportunity's creation date and the company signed date on the corresponding contract.

## Today's date: 2024-09-12
agent_sql:
WITH norm AS (
  SELECT
    ltrim(trim(o."OwnerId"), '#') AS owner_id,
    o."CreatedDate"::timestamptz AS opp_created,
    c."CompanySignedDate"::timestamptz AS signed
  FROM crmarenapro_opportunity o
  JOIN crmarenapro_contract c
    ON ltrim(trim(o."ContractID__c"), '#') = ltrim(trim(c."Id"), '#')
  WHERE c."CompanySignedDate" IS NOT NULL
    AND c."CompanySignedDate"::timestamptz >= '2023-04-01'
    AND c."CompanySignedDate"::timestamptz < '2023-05-01'
)
SELECT owner_id, avg(extract(epoch from signed - opp_created))/86400 AS avg_days
FROM norm
GROUP BY owner_id
ORDER BY avg_days ASC
LIMIT 1;

plan.keys: Opportunity.ContractID__c = Contract.Id after stripping leading '#' and whitespace from both sides (exact 1:1 key per hint).
plan.parse: normalize OwnerId and ContractID__c/Id with ltrim(trim(x),'#'); cast CreatedDate and CompanySignedDate text to timestamptz.
plan.filter: closing event (CompanySignedDate) falls in April 2023 [2023-04-01,2023-05-01), half-open; CompanySignedDate not null.
plan.metric: per agent (owner_id), average turnaround = avg(epoch seconds between CompanySignedDate and Opportunity CreatedDate)/86400, in days.

plan.shape: single row, agent Id only, as requested.

question:
Identify the agent who achieved the top sales figures for orders made in the past five months. Return only the Id of the agent.

## Sales Amount Policy
- Definition: The sales amount for an order is calculated as the product of the quantity and the unit price from the Order object (Quantity * UnitPrice). An opportunity is eligible if its associated contract has a company signed date that falls within the time interval of interest.

- Today's date: 2022-11-25
agent_sql:
with om as (
  select o."Id" as order_id, o."OwnerId" as owner_id, ct."Id" as contract_id, ct."CompanySignedDate"
  from crmarenapro_order o
  join crmarenapro_contract ct
    on ltrim(trim(o."AccountId"),'#')=ltrim(trim(ct."AccountId"),'#')
   and trim(o."EffectiveDate")=trim(ct."StartDate")
),
sales as (
  select om.order_id, om.owner_id, om."CompanySignedDate",
         sum(oi."Quantity"::numeric*oi."UnitPrice"::numeric) as amount
  from om
  join crmarenapro_orderitem oi on ltrim(trim(oi."OrderId"),'#')=ltrim(trim(om.order_id),'#')
  group by om.order_id, om.owner_id, om."CompanySignedDate"
)
select ltrim(trim(owner_id),'#') as agent_id, sum(amount) as total_sales
from sales
where trim("CompanySignedDate")::date >= date '2022-11-25' - interval '5 months'
  and trim("CompanySignedDate")::date <= date '2022-11-25'
group by agent_id
order by total_sales desc
limit 1;

    CASE 
      WHEN "Date" ~ '^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}' THEN substring("Date" from 1 for 10)::date

question: During 2018, how many businesses that received reviews offered either business parking or bike parking?
agent_sql:
with parsed as (
  select review_id, business_ref,
    case
      when date ~ '^[A-Za-z]+ [0-9]{2}, [0-9]{4} at [0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2} [AP]M$' and length(split_part(date,' ',1)) <= 3 then to_timestamp(date, 'Mon DD, YYYY at HH12:MI AM')
      when date ~ '^[A-Za-z]+ [0-9]{2}, [0-9]{4} at [0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2} [AP]M$' then to_timestamp(date, 'Month DD, YYYY at HH12:MI AM')
      when date ~ '^[0-9]{1,2} [A-Za-z]+ [0-9]{4}, [0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}$' and length(split_part(date,' ',2)) <= 3 then to_timestamp(date, 'DD Mon YYYY, HH24:MI')
      when date ~ '^[0-9]{1,2} [A-Za-z]+ [0-9]{4}, [0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}$' then to_timestamp(date, 'DD Month YYYY, HH24:MI')
      else date::timestamp
    end as ts
  from dataagentbench.yelp_review
),
r2018 as (
  select distinct business_ref from parsed where ts >= '2018-01-01' and ts < '2019-01-01'
)

from dataagentbench.yelp_business b
join r2018 r on b.business_id = 'businessid_' || split_part(r.business_ref,'_',2)
where (b.attributes->>'BikeParking' = 'True')

question: Which business category has the largest number of businesses that accept credit card payments, and what is its average rating?
agent_sql:
with base as (
  select business_id, description,
    attributes->>'BusinessAcceptsCreditCards' as cc,
    regexp_replace(description, '^.*?\y(?:AL|AK|AZ|AR|CA|CO|CT|DE|FL|GA|HI|ID|IL|IN|IA|KS|KY|LA|ME|MD|MA|MI|MN|MS|MO|MT|NE|NV|NH|NJ|NM|NY|NC|ND|OH|OK|OR|PA|RI|SC|SD|TN|TX|UT|VT|VA|WA|WV|WI|WY|DC|AB|BC|MB|NB|NL|NS|ON|PE|QC|SK|NT|NU|YT)\y[, ]*', '') as rest
  from dataagentbench.yelp_business
),
cats as (
  select distinct business_id, cc, (regexp_matches(rest, '[A-Z][A-Za-z'']*(?:\s*(?:&|/|-)\s*[A-Za-z][A-Za-z'']*|\s+(?:of|and)\s+[A-Z][A-Za-z'']*|\s+[A-Z][A-Za-z'']*|\s*\([A-Za-z]+\))*', 'g'))[1] as cat
  from base
),
cc_cats as (
  select distinct business_id, cat from cats where cc = 'True'
),
ranked as (
  select cat, count(*) as n_businesses,
         row_number() over (order by count(*) desc, cat asc) as rn
  from cc_cats
  group by cat
),
top_cat as (
  select cat, n_businesses from ranked where rn = 1
),
target_businesses as (
  select business_id from cc_cats where cat = (select cat from top_cat)
)
select tc.cat as category, tc.n_businesses,
       round(avg(r.rating),4) as avg_rating
from top_cat tc
join target_businesses t on true
join dataagentbench.yelp_review r on r.business_ref = 'businessref_' || split_part(t.business_id, '_', 2)
group by tc.cat, tc.n_businesses

question: Which business received the highest average rating between January 1, 2016 and June 30, 2016, and what category does it belong to? Consider only businesses with at least 5 reviews.
answer: Coffee House Too Cafe; categories: Restaurants, Breakfast & Brunch, American (New), Cafes (average rating 4.375 over 16 reviews Jan 1 - Jun 30, 2016)

agent_sql:
WITH parsed AS (
  SELECT review_id, business_ref, rating,
    CASE
      WHEN date ~ '^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}' THEN date::timestamp
      WHEN date ~ '^[0-9]+ [A-Za-z]+ [0-9]{4}, [0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}$' THEN to_timestamp(date, 'DD Mon YYYY, HH24:MI')
      WHEN date ~ '^[A-Za-z]+ [0-9]{2}, [0-9]{4} at [0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2} [AP]M$' THEN to_timestamp(date, 'Month DD, YYYY at HH12:MI AM')
    END AS ts
  FROM yelp_review
),
win AS (
  SELECT * FROM parsed WHERE ts >= '2016-01-01' AND ts < '2016-07-01'
),
agg AS (
  SELECT business_ref, avg(rating) avg_rating, count(*) cnt
  FROM win GROUP BY business_ref
  HAVING count(*) >= 5
)
SELECT b.name, a.avg_rating,
  regexp_replace(b.description, '^.*?, [A-Z]{2},?\s*(this|offers|located)?\s*(facility|establishment|location)?\s*(offers|providing)?', '') AS description
FROM agg a
JOIN yelp_business b ON b.business_id = replace(a.business_ref, 'businessref_', 'businessid_')
ORDER BY a.avg_rating DESC, a.cnt DESC, b.business_id ASC
LIMIT 1;

with tails as (
  select business_id, regexp_replace(description, '^.*?, [A-Z]{2}\y,?\s*', '') as tail
  from dataagentbench.yelp_business
),
segs as (
  select business_id, seg
  from tails, regexp_split_to_table(tail, ',') as seg
),
cats as (
  select business_id,
    (regexp_match(seg, '((?:[A-Z][A-Za-z]*|&|/|\([A-Za-z]+\))(?:[\s&/]+(?:[A-Z][A-Za-z]*|\([A-Za-z]+\)))*)'))[1] as cat
  from segs
),
biz_cats as (
  select distinct business_id, trim(cat) as category from cats where cat is not null
),
users2016 as (
  select user_id, yelping_since,
    case
      when yelping_since ~ '^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}' then substring(yelping_since from 1 for 4)::int
      when yelping_since ~ '^\d{1,2} [A-Za-z]{3} \d{4}' then extract(year from to_timestamp(yelping_since,'DD Mon YYYY, HH24:MI'))::int
      when yelping_since ~ '^[A-Za-z]+ \d{1,2}, \d{4}' then extract(year from to_timestamp(yelping_since,'Month DD, YYYY at HH12:MI AM'))::int
      else null
    end as reg_year
  from dataagentbench.yelp_user
),
u2016 as (select user_id from users2016 where reg_year = 2016),
rev as (
  select r.review_id, r.user_id, r.business_ref, r.date,
    case
      when r.date ~ '^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}' then to_timestamp(r.date,'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS')
      when r.date ~ '^\d{1,2} [A-Za-z]{3} \d{4}' then to_timestamp(r.date,'DD Mon YYYY, HH24:MI')
      when r.date ~ '^[A-Za-z]+ \d{1,2}, \d{4}' then to_timestamp(r.date,'Month DD, YYYY at HH12:MI AM')
      else null
    end as ts
  from dataagentbench.yelp_review r
  join u2016 on u2016.user_id = r.user_id
),
rev_since2016 as (
  select * from rev where ts >= '2016-01-01'
),
rev_biz as (
  select rev_since2016.*, 'businessid_' || split_part(business_ref,'_',2) as business_id
  from rev_since2016
)
select bc.category, count(*) as review_count
from rev_biz rb
join biz_cats bc on bc.business_id = rb.business_id
group by bc.category
order by review_count desc, bc.category asc
limit 5;
